about: What the FOCUS working group did on GitHub each day. Written each morning by an AI model from the day's comments, reviews, merges and closures, then fact-checked against them by a second call. It interprets, so check the threads before relying on it.

threads.title: AI #2847: Restructure the Editorial Guidelines and align the AGENTS.md grouping

days.text:
ijurica posted replies to most of jpradocueva's open review comments on #2848 (Restructure the Editorial Guidelines and align the AGENTS.md grouping), the draft pull request that moves rules into the new editorial-guidelines structure.

The line ijurica holds throughout is that the PR only relocates existing rules from #2847, so proposals that add new requirements stay on the working draft text for now. This applies to the subsection order rule, which would add a new MUST, with column subsection naming left to #2108. It also applies to first-occurrence linking, where ijurica agrees with the direction but says it needs separate rules for what counts as a reference, the appendix, glossary wording and section links. The inequality wording is deferred too, because "at least" appears in five requirements and counts need exclusions. The proposed number additions are postponed, listing issues such as inconsistent numerals across sentences. The entity ID naming proposal also stays on the working draft because some entities lack an ID section, though ijurica agrees grammatical number should never change an ID.

On comparisons, ijurica agrees with "be equal to" and suggests narrower wording for numeric values, but keeps the draft because the normative requirements guidance (NRG) uses "MUST equal" and both should change together.

ijurica accepted two things. The internal links rule is accepted as an exception to the scope of #2847 because it documents what the build already checks, with its scope stated in the rule, and a Glossary Link Targets rule is proposed alongside it. The colon in the number label is also moved inside the bold label, as in the other labels.

Several wording suggestions are waiting on jpradocueva. ijurica proposed rewording the exception placement rule so exceptions are clearly associated with and placed after the content they modify, and dropping "a single line of" from the single-line exception rule. For the Conventions rule, ijurica posted two options linking to the headings that notes sit under and asked which jpradocueva prefers. ijurica also proposed one merged Normative Requirements rule stating the boundary with the NRG, replacing the two sentences and the "Entity ID References" bullet, and suggested listing it as a scope exception. It is waiting on jpradocueva's agreement. Two other suggestions only propose deleting a line, and another adds an HTML comment marking a link target addition as not part of the proposal.

threads.title: [AI] Clarify relationship between BillingAccountId and ContractId

days.text:
#2887 (Clarify relationship between BillingAccountId and ContractId) has a new comment from ijurica proposing, as a discussion item, a separate Contract dataset. The proposal describes Agreement, Pricing and Commitment contracts, so that a price is defined once under a Pricing contract rather than repeated for each purchased commitment. It is marked as not part of the current specification.

The issue, opened by flanakin on 21 November, asks TF2 to settle how billing accounts, contracts and contract commitments relate in the SKU Price dataset, including whether a contract ID on commitment prices scopes price locks for an account or names a single commitment. No other replies are visible yet, so the thread is waiting on TF2's response to the proposal.

days.text:
Matt-Cowsert asked for targeted changes to #2826 (Period and Update Date Filtering for DatasetConfiguration), saying the new UpdatedSince rules contradict each other, so some rows are both required and forbidden in one delivery. The inline comments on dataset_configuration.md name several conflicts, including a latest-version rule that cannot sit alongside the all-rows rule when a row key has several versions, and a clause requiring rows that an exclusion forbids. Matt-Cowsert also raised the deduplication overlap handled in #2894 (Split Append delivery into Additive and Versioned Append), asked whether the schedule rule is a default or fixed, and asked whether the rules should reach every dataset. flanakin replied on 26 November by correcting the re-sent size estimates to about 7.0 GB and 3.5 GB, giving 3.0x and 11x, and applying the suggested wording to scenario 3. Replies to the rule conflicts are not yet in the thread.

Matt-Cowsert approved #2845 (Align SKU Price record wording across the SKU Price dataset), saying its six lines match the request, and approvals reached three. flanakin resolved the dataset.md discussion on 25 November, citing feedback and a TF2 agreement reached that day. No merge is recorded yet. On #2887 (Clarify relationship between BillingAccountId and ContractId), ijurica proposed that ContractId identify the source contract rather than a specific commitment, that billing accounts and contracts be treated as many-to-many until specified, and that the contract term be defined. It is the only comment so far.

seanmcilroy29, commenting for the Green Software Foundation, asked on #972 (Add granular sustainability dimensions and metrics) that FOCUS adopt the SCI, SWI and SEI definitions through an ISO normative reference rather than define its own, and offered collaboration and a possible supplemental dataset. No maintainer reply is recorded.

jpradocueva also opened two draft v1.5 release pull requests: #2904 (Merge working_draft into candidate_recommendation (Editorial changes) - FOCUS v1.5 Release), which carries agreed editorial and formatting fixes to RequesterDetails, and #2903 (FOCUS 1.5 Release - candidate_recommendation into main). Neither has reviews yet.

days.text:
#2871 (Add context-window pricing properties to SKU Price Details) now carries one String property for the provider's tier label, after Task Force 1 agreed on 24 November to drop the numeric bounds. Matt-Cowsert recorded the decision, saying the name avoids "Category" and "Type", and jerrysr99 will implement it. On the draft examples, jerrysr99 agreed that tier bounds must be whole numbers and that every meter in a tier, cache rows included, carries the same bounds. The maximum's null conditions are to be grouped, with the same change made in #2872. Matt-Cowsert leans toward keeping 0 as the lowest minimum after testing zero input tokens.

Matt-Cowsert's 24 November update on #2521 (Distinguish AI model costs by context window size) records the same swap. #2877 (Build a 1.6 example dataset for context window pricing) gained a link to SKU mapping material. Matt-Cowsert also opened #2901 (Open a feature request to improve the structure of SkuPriceDetails), assigned to ijurica and due 1 December, with no comments yet. Matt-Cowsert marked the AI item on #2850 (Compare SKU Price dataset columns with SkuPriceDetails properties) completed, though its feature requests still need Task Force 1 discussion.

ijurica has replied to several of jpradocueva's suggestions on #2848 (Restructure the Editorial Guidelines and align the AGENTS.md grouping). Subsection order and titles stay close to the working draft, with canonical order deferred to #2108. The entity ID naming rule is accepted with two added ID sections, and jpradocueva is asked to confirm. The thread is waiting on jpradocueva's answers. On #2842 (Add 1.4 to 1.5 migration guide), Matt-Cowsert applied a suggested lead-in sentence and removed a stray "and". Matt-Cowsert declined to add bullets for Commit Usage and Under Usage and Marketplace Purchases, since their 1.5 changes regroup existing queries rather than add new ones.

Matt-Cowsert moved #2899 (Publish the FOCUS 1.5 use cases and SQL queries to the FOCUS website) and #2898 (Publish the FOCUS 1.5 Data Model spreadsheet) to In Review, and neither has replies yet. On #2782 (Define the preview lifecycle for whole datasets), Matt-Cowsert reported that ijurica has started review of PR #2843, asking for precise FOCUS entities wording. Whether the requirements model can mark preview content is still to be confirmed. beau-finopsorg moved #2831 (Line up practitioners to review SKU Price sample data) and #2800 (Plan around 1.5 Preview Material - outbound and inbound) to In Progress. #2831 now has a tracking sheet, with outreach emails being prepared. Matt-Cowsert is deferring #2792 (Define the 1.6 engagement measures and Maintainer criteria) until after the new year, moving its due date to 18 January 2027.

beau-finopsorg also opened #2902 (Share activities around promotion of the FOCUS Mapping Tool with with Mike), asking for 5-6 promotion options, and has so far shared only a working document link. beau-finopsorg said #2694 (Audit the FOCUS-related contents on finops.org to see what actions are needed to prevent accidental dissociation with TF and IF) is deprioritised in favour of one-off changes, and it was closed as completed.

days.text:
jpradocueva left 32 inline comments on the draft restructuring of the Editorial Guidelines in #2848 (Restructure the Editorial Guidelines and align the AGENTS.md grouping), mostly proposing new or reworded rules on dashes, quotes, numbers, links, note labels, JSON and tables. No replies are recorded yet.

Several 1.5 specification pull requests also moved. #2853 (Correct the split cost allocation and commitment discount examples) gained qquigley's approval after Matt-Cowsert applied a suggestion in 8d07656f, but jpradocueva's em dash points, which break the Dash Usage rule, are unanswered. #2880 (Correct casing, IDs, and links in 1.5 requirement text) has qquigley's approval, while jpradocueva wants a Column ID in place of "allocation method". In #2869 (Correct metadata links, key names, and examples), Matt-Cowsert kept the FocusVersion fix jpradocueva made. #2881 (Skip null values in the 1.5 CommitmentDiscount allowed-values rules) has qquigley's approval, and #2842 (Add 1.4 to 1.5 migration guide) has flanakin's approval with small wording suggestions. In #2846 (Correct the Contract Commitment and commitment program examples), Matt-Cowsert relabelled the Datadog row and asked kk09v and ijurica whether that settles their questions. In #2830 (Add 1.5 Contributors), Matt-Cowsert told shawnalpay that one more contributor is added as an exception, another may follow if CLA steps finish by 2 December, and two stay off unless membership is confirmed. #2896 (Remove dependency loop from 1.5 Requirements Model) has qquigley's approval, but kk09v requested changes and opened #2900 (Remove dependency loop from 1.5 Requirements Model) as an alternative, arguing the other side of the loop should be narrowed.

#2844 (Create the FOCUS 1.5 Data Model spreadsheet) was closed as completed, with publishing moved to #2898 (Publish the FOCUS 1.5 Data Model spreadsheet), due 7 December. Matt-Cowsert asked rileyjenk and jpradocueva to review it. #2899 (Publish the FOCUS 1.5 use cases and SQL queries to the FOCUS website) lists 107 queries to go live by 9 December.

In #2730 (Enable magnitude abbreviations in Unit Format), Matt-Cowsert said the request needs refinement before estimation, and kk09v raised the ambiguity of M and suggested scientific notation such as 1E9. In #2885 (How should a non-invoicing metering layer (such as an LLM gateway) carry its computed cost when BilledCost and EffectiveCost must be 0?), andrasKelle says 1.4 leaves no compliant column for the estimate, and roy-tong suggests recording any migration explicitly. Matt-Cowsert set #2897 (Define path to mandatory, testable FOCUS metadata) to Needs More Info. ijurica proposed renaming the SKU Price dataset to Price List in #2856 (Clarify distinction between SKU Price construct and SKU Price records). flanakin's TF2 update on #2807 (Promote the SKU Price dataset to general availability) agreed that period filters return overlapping records. In #2742 (Enable comparing commitment discounts with on-demand rates), ijurica and flanakin agreed to track commitment ID links separately and want worked examples first. #2792 (Define the 1.6 engagement measures and Maintainer criteria) has its review moved from 23 to 30 November.

days.text:
Matt-Cowsert opened two threads on 22 November. #2897 (Define path to mandatory, testable FOCUS metadata) asks for metadata rules that are required rather than recommended, so a delivery can be marked pass or fail, and it has no comments yet. Pull request #2896 (Remove dependency loop from 1.5 Requirements Model) repoints one rule at CAU-SkuPriceId-C-001-M to break a circular dependency that stops focus-validator 2.2.1 from loading the 1.5 model. It has no approvals, reviews or comments yet, and Matt-Cowsert has set its task force to TF-Supporting and its PR type to Req Model.

undiscopurrr opened #2895 (Enable comparing delivered capacity with reserved capacity) on the same day. It asks for a column that states how much of a reserved charge counts as delivered, so that capacity made unavailable by host failures or maintenance is separated from capacity a customer chose not to use. It has had no replies.

days.text:
flanakin opened seven issues on 21 November that split the SKU Price general availability work under #2807 (Promote the SKU Price dataset to general availability) into tasks due between 25 November and 9 December. #2891 (Close SKU Price supported feature gaps) asks for queries to be run on three gaps found in #2879 (Add Azure practitioner scenarios to SKU Price supported features), with each gap then added or deferred with a reason. #2892 (Assess Storage Characteristics of Alternative SKU Price Models) is a size report on one price per row, with Microsoft figures so far and AWS and GCP still missing. #2893 (Provide SKU Price dataset complexity, size, and performance analysis) covers join complexity and query performance and goes to TF2 in draft first.

ijurica is assigned to four of the new issues. #2890 (Finalize columns needed for a SKU Price primary key) asks which columns guarantee uniqueness and what SKU Price ID should cover. #2887 (Clarify relationship between BillingAccountId and ContractId) asks TF2 to settle how billing accounts, contracts and commitments link, including many-to-many cases. #2889 (Finalize tiered pricing coverage in the SKU Price dataset) asks whether spend-based tiers block general availability. #2888 (Finalize where SKU properties live for SKU Price general availability), also assigned to finops-DaveMoreau, weighs placing SKU properties in SKU Price, in a SKU Details dataset, or in Cost and Usage alone. None of the seven has a comment yet.

flanakin's draft #2894 (Split Append delivery into Additive and Versioned Append) separates Additive Append, for new rows that practitioners sum, from Versioned Append, for newer versions of earlier rows that practitioners keep at the latest per row key. It is stacked on #2826 (Period and Update Date Filtering for DatasetConfiguration), and its description says that must merge first. On #2753 (Adding CommitmentApplicability to the SKU Price dataset), flanakin commented to record TF2's 18 November review, in which members asked to see the draft in practice. ijurica is asked for worked examples, before-and-after SKU Price ID views and a record-count and size comparison.

andrasKelle's #2885 (How should a non-invoicing metering layer (such as an LLM gateway) carry its computed cost when BilledCost and EffectiveCost must be 0?) asks how an LLM gateway should carry computed cost when those fields must be 0. roy-tong replied that BilledCost should stay absent rather than copy an estimate, that EffectiveCost should hold the best per-request figure, and that a provenance field should show whether a number came from an invoice or a local estimate. On #972 (Add granular sustainability dimensions and metrics), guillermollopis proposed optional estimated energy and location-based emissions columns for AI token rows, with a provenance field, and asked where they belong, what the default basis should be and whether kWh or joules is the right unit.

days.text:
ijurica disputes the origin-row wording in #2853 (Correct the split cost allocation and commitment discount examples), which flanakin approved on 20 November. ijurica's inline comments say a retained origin row rests on an assumption the normative text does not confirm, since "related to" is undefined and the nullability rules would fail. ijurica also asks that the field mapping example drop the origin row, and that #2515 be extended or #2578 be reopened, since #2578 was closed with two Definition of Done items not reflected. No reply from the author is recorded yet.

flanakin also approved #2846 (Correct the Contract Commitment and commitment program examples), #2870 (Correct summary tables, glossary entries, labels, and links), and #2869 (Correct metadata links, key names, and examples), all without a written comment. #2846 and #2870 now have three approvals each, and #2869 has one. On #2869, jpradocueva questioned the recency and schema dates on 17 November, and Matt-Cowsert changed them on 19 November.

Matt-Cowsert opened #2883 (Commitment discount scenario CSVs still use the removed ProviderName and PublisherName columns), saying all 14 scenario CSVs still carry them, and #2882 (Contract Commitment by Category query: unqualified ContractCommitmentId in GROUP BY fails on PostgreSQL-style engines), where the query fails with a binder error on DuckDB. andrasKelle asked in #2885 (How should a non-invoicing metering layer (such as an LLM gateway) carry its computed cost when BilledCost and EffectiveCost must be 0?) whether a gateway can carry computed cost in ListCost or ContractedCost. jpradocueva opened draft #2886 (AI 2847 reply to Irena proposal), which adds HTML review comments to the step-1 editorial guidelines.

rileyjenk commented on several threads. #2884 (One Participating Entity FR Definition To Rule Them All) proposes separating the participating-entity definitions, and #1226 (Review the use of "provider" vs "data generator") was marked a duplicate to be handled there. rileyjenk also said #1131 (Add machine-readable FOCUS column metadata) repeats existing metadata, and that #2294 (Define Billing Period population relative to Cost and Usage) is largely covered by recency. In reply to Matt-Cowsert on #2174 (Data Lineage Support - Distinguish data originators, processors, and intermediaries), rileyjenk noted that major cloud marketplaces bar payments made outside them. In #2704 (Clarification Request: Intended HostProviderName and ServiceProviderName Values for Sovereign Clouds (e.g., Azure operated by 21Vianet)), rileyjenk asked for an example of who the invoice is paid to.

days.text:
#2827 (Replace undefined Entry references with RequesterDetailsObject paths) and #2823 (Add spec.md in builds) merged on 19 November, after five and six approvals. On #2827, ijurica suggested flattening the list and asked whether line 43 should stay a MUST, and jpradocueva asked for a two-path form of that line. jpradocueva also reported that the group approved #2823 without objections on the 19 November members' call.

Matt-Cowsert asked for targeted changes in eight line comments on #2873 (Add ProcessingTier as a SkuPriceDetails property). The main point is that footnote 5 is the only statement of when ProcessingTier applies, and notes are non-normative, so Matt-Cowsert proposes MUST NOT and SHOULD bullets and a reworded footnote keyed to the SKU Price. Other comments note that the Standard rows in the Scenario A and B examples reuse SkuPriceIds from examples that carry no ProcessingTier, ask why Scenario B has no TokenCacheAction, propose that ProcessingTier should not set PricingCategory, and ask for the four providers offering Priority to be named. jerrysr99 asked whether processing tiers, quantity tiers and context-window ranges should follow one rule for SKU versus SKU Price, and welcomed Other and omission for varied provider data.

That SKU-versus-SKU Price question also comes up in #2871 (Add context-window pricing properties to SKU Price Details) and #2613 (Region scope as a SkuPriceDetails property). In #2871, a draft by jerrysr99, jerrysr99 agreed to rename the keys to TokenContextWindowMinimum and TokenContextWindowMaximum, carrying the change over to #2872 (Add context-window pricing columns to SKU Price (stacked on the properties PR)). jerrysr99 also proposed that null means an open end at both ends, allowed only for the lowest tier's minimum, the highest tier's maximum, or both for a SKU with no tiers. On the SKU question, jerrysr99 said the answer depends on how much weight the group gives to existing provider practice over pure design, and would give each range its own SkuId if the group agrees. On #2613, jerrysr99 prefers example values over a closed list for RegionScope.

flanakin's four inline comments on dataset.md in #2826 (Period and Update Date Filtering for DatasetConfiguration) spell out the changed-since rules: delivery uses the Append mechanism explicitly, corrections that change a record's key need a delivery without a changed-since point, scheduled deliveries advance the cutoff to the previous delivery's capture time, and retirements set an end date and update SkuPriceLastUpdated. Each is marked as AI-generated.

ijurica suggested two commented-out additions to editorial-guidelines-restructuring-step-1.md in #2848 (Restructure the Editorial Guidelines and align the AGENTS.md grouping): table of contents entries and a heading for Supported Features Editorial Rules, plus Retired Rule IDs (Optional). flanakin also opened draft #2879 (Add Azure practitioner scenarios to SKU Price supported features), a spec-only change adding common price scenarios such as comparing list and contracted prices.

jerrysr99 revised #2871 (Add context-window pricing properties to SKU Price Details) on 15 November, applying six of thecloudman's suggestions as written and the rest with changes. thecloudman's review had checked that both example CSVs reconcile, then objected that the MUST nullability wording made ContextWindowMinimum and ContextWindowMaximum mandatory on a generally available dataset, against the SHOULD level noted at TF1. jerrysr99 restored the existing MAY-be-null rule, moved both keys to SHOULD, and added that the maximum SHOULD NOT appear without the minimum. The one-value bullets and the restated type lines were removed, and the bounds now follow each provider's own count, worded "toward the threshold in its pricing terms".

Two points go to TF1. jerrysr99 kept the explicit null for an unbounded maximum, footnoted it, and listed it as open question 4, after thecloudman asked whether it was needed at all. On the 127999 boundary value in the examples, jerrysr99 partly agreed: the conversion rule is in footnote 5 but not yet normative, so both of thecloudman's options go to TF1 as open question 7. The SkuPriceId naming in the examples is now marked illustrative, and a sentence on Meridian AI cache-write tokens has been added. The SKU Price columns and their one-value-per-SkuPriceId requirements sit in #2872 (Add context-window pricing columns to SKU Price (stacked on the properties PR)), where the same change was made.

Separately, thecloudman opened #2873 (Add ProcessingTier as a SkuPriceDetails property), which adds ProcessingTier with five allowed values: the three already in the request, plus Flex and Other, with a footnote and examples. It contributes to #2437 (Distinguish AI inference processing tiers), opened by Matt-Cowsert on 2 June, which thecloudman now champions. In a comment on #2437, thecloudman said the first contribution targets workingdraftinterim for 1.6 and asked Task Force 2 about the value set, the boundary for provisioned capacity, and whether the property belongs on SKU or SKU Price. #2873 is open.

days.text:
qquigley dropped the seven-day no-objection window from #2859 (Separate Champion scope entry from PR approval) and answered the rest of Matt-Cowsert's review points in five replies to development-processes.md. After sponsorship, Maintainers confirm readiness at a Maintainers meeting, and a not-ready decision keeps the Feature Request in Champion scope with the sponsorship standing. qquigley said the window had been added without the context of the 9 November meeting and that the process would be adjusted to match that practice. Scope will now change when a contributor commits in a comment on the FR to lead the work, with the WG Chair setting it to Champion, and the champion's comments will be split in two as suggested. Both must lines are confirmed as requirements, the objection bullet is removed, and held Feature Requests stay off Task Force agendas until Maintainers decide. On approvals, qquigley said an approval already means ready to merge for every PR, so early approvals need no special rule.

jerrysr99 opened two draft PRs for the joint solution to #2521 (Distinguish AI model costs by context window size). #2871 (Add context-window pricing properties to SKU Price Details) adds ContextWindowMinimum and ContextWindowMaximum to SkuPriceDetails, the Cost and Usage half. #2872 (Add context-window pricing columns to SKU Price (stacked on the properties PR)) is stacked on #2871 and adds the same two bounds as Conditional columns in SKU Price, along with an IncludesContextWindowPricing condition, SkuPriceId requirements and a worked appendix example. On #2872, jerrysr99 also posted a snapshot of providers and models with context-window pricing as of 9 November, quoting threshold wording only. On #2521, jerrysr99 listed six ways context window size can affect pricing and found only whole-request application among the provider pages reviewed.

#2845 (Align SKU Price record wording across the SKU Price dataset) has two approvals, from ijurica and flanakin, after finops-DaveMoreau changed six lines to name the record. ijurica would merge it as written, with broader terminology work split out. kk09v's objection, asking whether "record" should join the glossary, was answered as out of scope for this pull request.

ijurica also opened three SKU Price naming issues. #2856 (Clarify distinction between SKU Price construct and SKU Price records) asks whether to keep the name, rename the dataset, or rename its record-level columns. #2855 (Align pricing terminology across the SKU Price dataset, its appendix, and its supported features) proposes glossary-based pricing terms and overlaps #2845. #2854 (Revisit the SKU Price Description column) asks whether that column describes the SKU Price or a record. #2855 and #2854 are both set to TF-Core 2. In #1027 (Rename "Charge" row term to just "Row"), kk09v notes that "record" already names the same concept in the SKU Price dataset, leaving three terms. The draft #2828 (Simplify scoped detail to user-defined column rules) received an inline suggestion from Matt-Cowsert on summable custom columns.

Matt-Cowsert opened #2853 (Correct the split cost allocation and commitment discount examples) to fix example figures without changing requirements. #2852 (Decide how the Columns table and the Requirements column list count for first-occurrence linking) asks the group to decide the linking rule. #2851 (Reword "term" in the Commitment Discount Quantity requirement) asks whether "term" becomes "period", a change that would move to 1.6. In #2827 (Replace undefined Entry references with RequesterDetailsObject paths), jerrysr99 backed deferring the binding to #2838 (State how repeated [*] paths bind to array elements in JSON object requirements). In #2770 (Define review artifact process), Matt-Cowsert says section 5.3 of the Operating Procedures in the Foundation repository is now merged, so the guidelines cite it rather than waiting for ratification. ljadvey closed #2777 (Slim AGENTS.md to defer to contributor guidelines (less is more)) without merging, in favor of #2848 (Restructure the Editorial Guidelines and align the AGENTS.md grouping).

jerrysr99 approved #2749 (Add SkuMeter to SkuPrice dataset) and #2748 (Add QuantityTierCategory to SkuPrice dataset), and both now have three approvals. Matt-Cowsert also gave two 1.6 inputs on #2698 (Decide Version Updated policy and apply consistently), noting that #2766's files still say Version Updated 1.4.

days.text:
#2847 (Restructure the Editorial Guidelines and align the AGENTS.md grouping) was closed as completed on 10 November after Matt-Cowsert reported the initial draft done, though some rebase is expected. ijurica opened the draft #2848 (Restructure the Editorial Guidelines and align the AGENTS.md grouping) to carry the work forward, and closed #2765 (Review changes to entity reference and linking rules proposed in #2514) without merging it. In #2806 (Consolidate findings on gaps and conflicts in the contributor guidelines), ijurica drafted an Action Item, not yet an issue, asking whether column values should use double quotes or backticks, what happens to Consistent Formatting, and whether MUST or SHOULD applies. Matt-Cowsert moved its due date to 17 November. Matt-Cowsert closed #2240 (Use backticks instead of double-quotes for all string column values) as no action needed, citing possible overlap with the 1.6 editorial changes.

finops-DaveMoreau's pull request #2845 (Align SKU Price record wording across the SKU Price dataset) changes six lines to name the record and closes #2735 (Align the SKU Price record wording across the SKU Price dataset). In a comment, finops-DaveMoreau said the wording fits the #2725 rule but suggested renaming the dataset, perhaps to Price List in a later version. Matt-Cowsert closed #2751 (Explore how SKU Price can express usage covered by commitment discounts) as complete, but the group review is held until 18 November. Matt-Cowsert also opened #2850 (Compare SKU Price dataset columns with SkuPriceDetails properties) for TF-Core 1. On #2521 (Distinguish AI model costs by context window size), Task Force 1 agreed to recommend carrying the bounds in both SKU Price and SkuPriceDetails, based on a draft by jerrysr99. #2335 (Revise Feature Levels to make FOCUS more globally applicable) returned to Seeking Champion for 1.6.

Matt-Cowsert took Task Force 1 through open questions in the draft PR #2843 (Define the preview lifecycle for whole datasets), which underpins #2782 (Define the preview lifecycle for whole datasets). #2770 (Define review artifact process) moved to TF-Supporting. On #2776 (Label Version Introduced with GA), jpradocueva resolved an inline comment on dataset.md without requesting a change. Matt-Cowsert opened #2846 (Correct the Contract Commitment and commitment program examples), which fixes examples and descriptions without changing requirement lines. Matt-Cowsert also opened #2849 (Track the 1.5 errata from Maintainer assessment to one errata PR) to follow #2836 (Correct casing, IDs, and links in 1.5 requirement text), #2837 (Correct the Payment Currency, Contract ID, and Time Sector End requirements) and #2783 through to a single errata PR. #2844 (Create the FOCUS 1.5 Data Model spreadsheet) is due 17 November and now in progress.

Matt-Cowsert closed #2818 (Open a Champion scope feature request for review artifacts), #2795 (Open a feature request for Version Introduced and Version Updated semantics), #2767 (Conduct 1.5 retrospective) and #1545 (Generate list of considerations of what might unlock adoption) as complete, without further detail. The Maintainers' 9 November call closed #2603 (Add specification-level privacy and data protection statement), since providers and customers protect sensitive data, though it can be reopened. On #2174 (Data Lineage Support - Distinguish data originators, processors, and intermediaries), participants said who changed each row matters most, and disagreed about whether lineage depends on #1060 and #1131 (Add machine-readable FOCUS column metadata).

days.text:
Matt-Cowsert closed #2603 (Add specification-level privacy and data protection statement) as completed. Matt-Cowsert said the topic came up on the 9 November Maintainers call and was acknowledged as important, but is outside what FOCUS should define.

Two pull requests were closed without merging as part of the outreach on open pull requests for 1.6. Matt-Cowsert closed #2564 (Add tiered-pricing-related glossary terms) after ijurica agreed it could wait. It can be reopened if #2839 makes 1.6, and the branch is kept. #2357 (Adding Development Process Supporting Content - FOCUS 1.5 Operating Model Augmentation Discussion) was closed at ijurica's request, because the Candidate Release had already been cleared. Its branch also stays in place.

Matt-Cowsert opened #2844 (Create the FOCUS 1.5 Data Model spreadsheet), which would build the 1.5 spreadsheet from v1.5-cr, add SKU Price and four columns with operating model conditions, and leave open choices for Maintainers to settle. Matt-Cowsert also opened a draft pull request, #2843 (Define the preview lifecycle for whole datasets), as a starting point for the feature request #2782 (Define the preview lifecycle for whole datasets). It adds proposed answers and TODO markers to the Preview Process in the spec change guidelines, and changes no specification text yet.

On #2820 (Demonstrate reusable scope rule evaluation in supported features), ijurica replied to a triage comment by Matt-Cowsert. ijurica said "reusable" means reuse across supported features rather than across columns, named the two columns in scope, and flagged the null-dimension In and NotIn cases as open. ijurica also moved #2806 (Consolidate findings on gaps and conflicts in the contributor guidelines) to In Progress.
